canonical_name: Linux TCP congestion control -- CUBIC and BBR (the congestion-avoidance lineage under pressure)
lineage: TCP congestion control (1988-, Van Jacobson onward): Tahoe -> Reno -> NewReno -> CUBIC (2008, loss-based, the Linux default) -> BBR (2016, Google, model-based rate/RTT). Each redesign was forced by a changed network: higher bandwidth-delay products, then bufferbloat. Preserved here as the actual Linux kernel modules tcp_cubic.c and tcp_bbr.c.
dependencies: the Linux kernel TCP stack (struct tcp_sock, the congestion_ops interface)
entry_points: struct tcp_congestion_ops: .cong_avoid / .ssthresh / .cong_control (cubic); the BBR state machine (STARTUP/DRAIN/PROBE_BW/PROBE_RTT)

human_capability_summary.built_to: regulate a TCP sender's transmission rate so it uses available bandwidth without collapsing the shared network -- inferring congestion from loss (CUBIC) or from a bandwidth/RTT model (BBR)
human_capability_summary.pressure: a shared link of unknown, varying capacity with many competing senders; too fast causes loss and congestion collapse, too slow wastes the link
human_capability_summary.success_means: high throughput, low queueing delay, and fairness to other flows across a range of bandwidth-delay products and loss rates

known_human_problem_solved: congestion avoidance on a shared network
human_environmental_pressure: bandwidth scarcity, packet loss, variable RTT, bufferbloat, competing flows
human_failure_condition: congestion collapse (1986): everyone retransmits into a saturated link and useful throughput drops toward zero
behavioral_entry_point: the two files ARE the before/after of a documented redesign: CUBIC's loss-triggered cubic window vs BBR's explicit bandwidth+RTT probing. Read them side by side; a live study injects loss/delay with netem.

lineage_relations.note: CUBIC replaced Reno-family as Linux default
the congestion-avoidance lineage all descend from

versions_preserved.role: TRANSITION -- loss-based, replaced Reno/BIC as the Linux default
AFTER -- model-based, a paradigm change from loss-triggered to rate/RTT estimation

versions_preserved.note: BEFORE (Tahoe/Reno/NewReno, 1988-1999) referenced but not preserved here; queued from historical BSD
